author: blu
body: An MQTT v5 client on a real socket, so that something other than our own loopback can be the thing that answers it.

author: blu
body: THE RECORD BOUNDARY IS THE WHOLE OF THE TRANSPORT WORK, exactly as it is for TLS. `mqtt-ep-recv` takes a buffer and answers how many bytes it consumed; TCP delivers whatever happened to arrive, so a segment may hold half a packet or three. The loop keeps the remainder.

author: blu
body: Read once, feed everything complete out of the buffer, keep the rest. The step reports the byte count it took, and the remainder is carried forward -- this is the only place in the client that can desynchronise the stream, so it is the only place that decides how much was consumed.

author: blu
body: Publish, then pump until the broker has finished with it. A QoS 1 exchange is one round trip and a QoS 2 exchange is two, so the pump runs until the endpoint reports the publish retired rather than a fixed number of times -- a count that happened to suit QoS 1 would report a QoS 2 publish as unacknowledged when it was merely halfway.

author: blu
body: The rounds are bounded. A broker that stops answering must end the run with `acked=False`, which the harness fails on; looping until success would turn a broken exchange into a hang.
